extracted.intended_audience: Users of the GAP computer algebra system (mathematicians and programmers working with finite fields, abelian number fields, and vector spaces in GAP)
extracted.subtask_short: GAP reference: fields and vector spaces
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for GAP functions, properties, and methods related to finite fields, abelian number fields, Galois actions, and vector-space/basis operations; describes constructors, attributes, and behaviors with usage notes and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display / ViewObj formatting for large finite-field elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements of larger finite fields are printed as sums of low powers of the primitive root (GAP expressions) or in a compact zi/kzi notation for Display/ViewObj. ViewObj uses the compact form only if its length does not exceed the user preference ViewLength; longer output is replaced by <<an element of GF(p,d)>>. Elements of large prime fields are stored and displayed as residue class objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show Print and Display outputs; Display always uses the compact z-notation. ViewObj uses compact form conditionally (based on ViewLength). For very large fields Display can materialize a long sum of zi terms; ViewObj may hide it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Abelian number field (GAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: An abelian number field is a finite-dimensional normal extension of the prime field in characteristic zero whose Galois group is abelian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAP's implementation for abelian number fields is given by fields of cyclotomic numbers (IsCyclotomic). Functions in this chapter are developed for fields in the filter IsCyclotomic and may not work well for abelian number fields built from other kinds of elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: CyclotomicField / CF constructors
rubrics_metrics.description: CyclotomicField([subfield,] n) creates the n-th cyclotomic field Q_n; CyclotomicField([subfield,] gens) creates the smallest cyclotomic field containing elements in gens. CF is abbreviation used for printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-argument versions allow specifying a subfield to represent the field as an extension. Fields constructed with the one-argument version are stored in the global list CYCLOTOMIC_FIELDS so repeated calls fetch existing objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: AbelianNumberField / NF constructor
rubrics_metrics.description: AbelianNumberField(n, stab) (abbreviated NF) returns the fixed field of the group described by stab (a list of prime residues modulo n) inside the n-th cyclotomic field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mainly intended for internal use and for producing a standard printed representation; Field(...) is probably more suitable if generators of the field are known. Fields constructed with NF are stored in global ABELIAN_NUMBER_FIELDS and are fetched on repeated calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: GaussianRationals and IsGaussianRationals
rubrics_metrics.description: GaussianRationals is the global object representing Q(i) as cyclotomic numbers. IsGaussianRationals(obj) returns true exactly for the GaussianRationals object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CF(4) equals GaussianRationals; Sqrt(-1) is an element of GaussianRationals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors over abelian number fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors(F) for polynomials over abelian number fields (cyclotomics) works in principle but may be inefficient if the degree of the field extension is large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples compare factoring over rationals vs over CF(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsNumberField property
rubrics_metrics.description: IsNumberField(F) returns true if F is a finite-dimensional extension of a prime field in characteristic zero, false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to detect number fields vs finite fields etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsAbelianNumberField property
rubrics_metrics.description: IsAbelianNumberField(F) returns true if F is a number field that is a Galois extension of the prime field with abelian Galois group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relies on GaloisGroup computations (see GaloisGroup).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsCyclotomicField property
rubrics_metrics.description: IsCyclotomicField(F) returns true if F is a cyclotomic field: an abelian number field that can be generated by roots of unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show true for CF(9) and Field([Sqrt(-3)]), false for Field([Sqrt(3)]).

rubrics_metrics.name: GaloisStabilizer attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: GaloisStabilizer(F) returns the set of integers k in [1..n] (where n is the conductor) such that the automorphism raising n-th roots of unity to the k-th power acts trivially on F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to describe subfields of cyclotomic fields; example shows computing stabilizer for Field([sqrt(5)]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vector-space representation of abelian number fields / LeftActingDomain
rubrics_metrics.description: Each abelian number field F is a vector space over Q (or over Q_n if F contains Q_n). A field object represents a vector-space object over a certain subfield S; S is available as LeftActingDomain(F). CanonicalBasis(F) returns Zumbroich/Lenstra/normal S-bases depending on the construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior of CanonicalBasis depends on whether S is cyclotomic or not; NF and two-argument CF return vector spaces over Q, respectively over the specified subfield.

rubrics_metrics.name: CanonicalBasis for cyclotomic fields (Zumbroich basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F = Q_n represented as a vector space over Q_m (m | n) then CanonicalBasis(F) returns the Zumbroich basis consisting of E(n)^i for i in ZumbroichBase(n,m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ZumbroichBase is given by an explicit combinatorial construction based on prime powers dividing n and m; the basis is integral, normal for squarefree n, and closed under complex conjugation for odd n.

rubrics_metrics.name: CanonicalBasis for NF(n,stab) (Lenstra basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F = NF(n, stab) and represented over Q_m then CanonicalBasis(F) returns the Lenstra basis (sums of roots of unity described by LenstraBase(n,stab,stab,m)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LenstraBase returns lists of exponents whose sums form an integral basis of NF(n,stab) over Q_m; if possible the result is chosen compatible with a 'super' group action. stabilizer must not contain stabilizer of a proper cyclotomic subfield (conductor constraint).

rubrics_metrics.name: ZumbroichBase(n,m) function
rubrics_metrics.description: ZumbroichBase(n, m) returns the set of exponents i for which E(n)^i belongs to the generalized Zumbroich basis of Q_n viewed as a vector space over Q_m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition given via prime-power decomposition of n and combinatorial choices; notes on special case n ≡ 2 (mod 4). Provides examples for small n,m.

rubrics_metrics.name: LenstraBase(n, stabilizer, super, m) function
rubrics_metrics.description: LenstraBase returns a list of integer-lists [b1,...,bk] such that sums ∑_{j in bi} E(n)^j form a basis of NF(n,stabilizer) as a vector space over the m-th cyclotomic field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The basis is integral. If possible chosen so that the super group acts consistently. Example outputs illustrate bases and orbits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galois action on cyclotomic fields (GaloisCyc)
rubrics_metrics.description: Field automorphisms of Q_n are given by linear maps *k defined by E(n)^*k = E(n)^k for gcd(n,k)=1. In GAP this image is computed by GaloisCyc(z,k). For gcd(n,k)≠1 the map is Q-linear but not a field automorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show that (E(5)+E(5)^4)^2 and its image under GaloisCyc differ; using GaloisCyc with k not coprime to n gives linear maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: GaloisGroup for abelian number fields
rubrics_metrics.description: GaloisGroup(F) returns the Galois group of Q_n (or of subextensions) described via (Z/nZ)^* and factor/subgroups corresponding to stabilizers. Generators can be computed using GeneratorsPrimeResidues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galois groups in GAP are represented as permutation/actions objects; examples show Size, IsCyclic, IsAbelian, and action on normal bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: ANFAutomorphism(F,k)
rubrics_metrics.description: ANFAutomorphism returns the automorphism of an abelian number field F defined by raising each root of unity in F to its k-th power; k must be coprime to the conductor of F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ANFAutomorphism(CF(25),2) returns automorphism of order 20; can be composed and queried via Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: GaussianIntegers and IsGaussianIntegers
rubrics_metrics.description: GaussianIntegers is the global ring Z[i] as a subring of GaussianRationals; IsGaussianIntegers(obj) is the defining category that identifies this domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used where Gaussian integer arithmetic/structures are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsLeftVectorSpace / IsVectorSpace category
rubrics_metrics.description: A vector space in GAP is a free left module over a division ring. IsLeftVectorSpace and IsVectorSpace are synonyms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The left-acting division ring (coefficient domain) is accessible as LeftActingDomain(V). All GAP vector spaces are left vector spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: VectorSpace(F, gens[, zero][, "basis"])
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs the F-vector space spanned by gens. Optional zero argument supplies the zero element if gens is empty. Optional string "basis" indicates gens are known to be linearly independent (so dimension set immediately).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If "basis" is provided, Basis need not return the same vector list; it only sets dimension without extra checks. Example shows creating vector space over Rationals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subspace(V, gens[, "basis"]) and SubspaceNC
rubrics_metrics.description: Subspace returns the F-vector subspace of V spanned by gens (parent set to V). SubspaceNC omits the check whether gens ⊆ V. The optional "basis" string indicates gens are known linearly independent so checks are omitted and dimension is set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If gens is empty the trivial subspace is returned. Use SubspaceNC for performance when caller guarantees membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: AsVectorSpace(F, D)
rubrics_metrics.description: If elements of domain D form an F-vector space then AsVectorSpace returns that F-vector space, otherwise fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to view a given vector space as a vector space over a smaller or larger division ring. Example shows converting GF(3^3)^3 to GF(3)-vector space (dimension multiplies).

rubrics_metrics.name: AsSubspace(V, U)
rubrics_metrics.description: If U is a subset of V whose elements form an F-vector space then AsSubspace returns that vector space with parent set to V; otherwise fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to coerce collections into subspace objects when appropriate; example shows success and fail cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: GeneratorsOfLeftVectorSpace
rubrics_metrics.description: GeneratorsOfLeftVectorSpace(V) returns a list of vectors that generate V as an F-vector space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonly used to inspect or reconstruct vector spaces; example provides canonical generators for full row space over rationals.

rubrics_metrics.name: TrivialSubspace
rubrics_metrics.description: TrivialSubspace(V) returns the zero subspace of V (dimension 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows AsSet(triv) returning the zero vector explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subspaces(V[, k]) domain
rubrics_metrics.description: Subspaces(V) returns the domain of all subspaces of finite vector space V; Subspaces(V, k) returns the domain of all k-dimensional subspaces. Special Size and Iterator methods exist for these domains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows iterating over Subspaces(GF(3)^3) and counting Size.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSubspacesVectorSpace category
rubrics_metrics.description: The domain returned by Subspaces belongs to category IsSubspacesVectorSpace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify domains representing collections of subspaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis concept in GAP
rubrics_metrics.description: A basis B = [v1,...,vn] of a free left F-module V is a list of vectors that generate V and are linearly independent; length of list equals dimension. Basis objects support operations like BasisVectors, Coefficients, LinearCombination, UnderlyingLeftModule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basis operations defined only for finite dimensional vector spaces in practice (dimension not exceeding a few hundred).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsBasis property
rubrics_metrics.description: IsBasis(obj) returns true for objects that are basis objects (immutable lists that know how to compute coefficients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A plain list of vectors is not IsBasis; Basis(...) constructs proper basis objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis(V[, vectors]) and BasisNC
rubrics_metrics.description: Basis(V) with no vectors returns a basis object; Basis(V, vectors) returns the basis when vectors form an F-basis, otherwise fail. BasisNC omits checks (assumes vectors are a basis). If no vectors specified, basis vectors may be computed on first call to BasisVectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows Basis returning SemiEchelonBasis and BasisVectors computing vectors lazily. Basis(V, vectors) validates the input unless NC variant used.

rubrics_metrics.name: CanonicalBasis(V)
rubrics_metrics.description: If V supports a canonical basis then CanonicalBasis(V) returns it; canonical bases are uniquely determined by V and allow equality checks between vector spaces via basis comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canonical bases are defined for various V types (e.g., Gaussian row/matrix spaces, certain finite-field bases). Implementers must ensure CanonicalBasis methods do not call Basis; recommended to have Basis call CanonicalBasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: RelativeBasis(B, vectors) and RelativeBasisNC
rubrics_metrics.description: RelativeBasis checks whether vectors form a basis of the same free left module V as B and returns a basis object that delegates computations to another basis via basechange matrices; RelativeBasisNC omits the check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to create bases whose heavy lifting is delegated to a precomputed basis and a basechange matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: BasisVectors(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: BasisVectors(B) returns the list of basis vectors of basis object B; equivalent to B itself, but provided as attribute access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to extract a plain list of vectors from a basis object without exposing underlying module semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: UnderlyingLeftModule(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: UnderlyingLeftModule(B) returns the free left module V for which B is a basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basis objects store their underlying module so that membership checks and delayed-basis computations are possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coefficients(B, v)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coefficients(B, v) returns the list of coefficients of vector v w.r.t. basis B if v ∈ V (the underlying module), otherwise fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to test membership and to recover coordinates; example demonstrates success and fail cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: LinearCombination(B, coeff)
rubrics_metrics.description: LinearCombination(B, coeff) returns the vector sum_i coeff[i] * B[i] for basis B (or homogeneous list) and row-vector coeff of same length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary use is to convert coordinate vectors into actual vectors in V.

rubrics_metrics.name: EnumeratorByBasis(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: EnumeratorByBasis(B) returns an enumerator that loops over elements of V as linear combinations of basis vectors B with coefficients taken from the full row space of appropriate dimension, in the default succession of that row space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows enumerating first 4 elements for GF(2)^3 using CanonicalBasis and a custom basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: IteratorByBasis(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: IteratorByBasis(B) returns an iterator performing the same traversal as EnumeratorByBasis but as an iterator object (NextIterator returns next element).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate iteration over the vector space elements in a defined order for different bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsCanonicalBasis(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsCanonicalBasis(B) returns true if the underlying module supports a canonical basis and B equals that canonical basis, false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to check whether a basis is the unique canonical one for comparisons and canonicalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsIntegralBasis(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsIntegralBasis(B) returns true if an S-basis B of a field F is also an R-basis of the ring of integers M of F, where R is the ring of integers of S (i.e., basis yields integral coordinates exactly for algebraic integers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when working with integral structures of number fields (e.g., Lenstra/Zumbroich integral bases).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsNormalBasis(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsNormalBasis(B) returns true if the S-basis B of field F is invariant under the Galois group of the extension F/S, false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to detect normal bases (Galois-orbit bases). Example shows testing canonical basis of GaussianRationals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutable basis concept and categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Mutable bases are mutable objects representing a basis for a free module that can be extended/closed with new vectors without creating new module/basis objects; mutable bases are in category IsMutableBasis and are not lists but collections whose family equals the family of their basis vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutable bases differ from immutable bases: they cannot store attributes; ShallowCopy returns a mutable plain list of current basis vectors. There are generic mutable bases that store an immutable basis, mutable bases that store a mutable basis for a nicer module, and special mutable bases using problem-specific information (e.g., Gaussian row/matrix spaces).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsMutableBasis(MB)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsMutableBasis(MB) indicates whether MB is a mutable basis object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to dispatch mutable-basis-specific operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: MutableBasis(R, vectors[, zero])
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs a mutable basis for the R-free module generated by vectors; optional zero supplies zero vector if vectors is empty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that vectors passed may not be the actual basis vectors stored internally; MutableBasis attempts to be efficient for building bases incrementally.

rubrics_metrics.name: NrBasisVectors(MB)
rubrics_metrics.description: NrBasisVectors(MB) returns the current number of basis vectors stored in the mutable basis MB (not an attribute because the value changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as equivalent of Dimension for mutable bases during incremental construction; example shows value 1 for certain input due to linear dependence reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: ImmutableBasis(MB[, V])
rubrics_metrics.description: ImmutableBasis returns an immutable basis B with the same basis vectors as the mutable basis MB. If V is provided it sets UnderlyingLeftModule(B) = V; useful when a nicer module is known in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows extracting a stable immutable basis from a mutable construction for further use.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsContainedInSpan(MB, v)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsContainedInSpan(MB, v) returns true if vector v lies in the R-span of the current basis vectors of mutable basis MB, false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cheap membership test used during incremental closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: CloseMutableBasis(MB, v)
rubrics_metrics.description: CloseMutableBasis(MB, v) modifies mutable basis MB so that afterwards MB describes the span of the former basis vectors together with v (i.e., closes under adding v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to incrementally extend the basis; implementation may update internal structures to maintain efficiency.
